metadata.agent_last_message:
Implemented a full Node.js CLI BibTeX-style processor at [output/main.js](/workspace/output/main.js).

What it now does:

- Accepts `--bib`, `--style`, `--cites`, `--aux`, `--output`, `--log`.
- Parses `.bib` (`@entry`, `@string`, `@preamble`, `@comment`), macro concatenation with `#`, predefined month macros, duplicate key detection, unresolved macro warnings.
- Parses `.bst` commands (`ENTRY`, `STRINGS`, `INTEGERS`, `FUNCTION`, `MACRO`, `READ`, `EXECUTE`, `ITERATE`, `REVERSE`, `SORT`) and function literals.
- Executes a BibTeX-style stack machine with built-ins needed by canonical styles (`plain/alpha/unsrt/abbrv`), including formatting and control flow (`format.name$`, `num.names$`, `change.case$`, `purify$`, `width$`, `text.length$`, `text.prefix$`, `substring$`, `if$`, `while$`, etc.).
- Implements crossref inheritance and warnings (`unresolved_crossref`, `crossref_cycle`).
- Produces `.bbl` via `write$`/`newline$` with LF endings and 79-column wrapping.
- Writes structured log JSON when `--log` is provided.
- On failure, writes required error JSON to `--output` and exits with required exit codes (`0/1/2`).

Validation I ran:

- `node --check /workspace/output/main.js`
- End-to-end runs with canonical styles (`plain.bst`, `alpha.bst`, `abbrv.bst`) against sample `.bib`/cite inputs.
- Verified success path output `.bbl`, log counters, warnings, and failure-path error JSON.
